leads.name: Hungarian oak, Beningbrough Hall estate yard (NT)
leads.reason: 2026-11-04 verify pass: Yorkshire Post (search result; page 403 to fetch) says it is a Tree Register Yorkshire champion for height and girth, plus a cockscomb beech (American Garden, girth), a cherry (Cherry Lawn, girth) and a whitebeam (playground, height). No measurement seen, no coordinate, no public-transport link within ~30 min of York found; Tree Register record needed. Lead: no photo or exact pin in reach.

leads.name: Sequoia (giant redwood), York Cemetery, Cemetery Road
leads.reason: 2026-11-04: one passing quote in Yorkshire Post (a staff member says the cemetery has a sequoia); no height, girth, age or position. Victorian Web also names surviving false acacia and tulip trees from before 1979 with no individual tree. Historic England list entry 1001596 mentions a lime-bordered drive south of the chapel. No named individual to pin. Lead.

leads.reason: 2026-11-04: named on York Museum Gardens plants page with no size or age; Wollemi pine is a young planting. Not remarkable on current evidence.

blocked.name: Eye of York oak (Castle Gateway, between Clifford's Tower and Castle Museum)
blocked.reason: About 40 years old per York Mix 2021 (planted for an MP's anniversary, one source); beloved and kept after public vote, but young. Not ancient or spectacular by size.
